title: Discovery — Meridian Robotics SDR Outbound & Contact Data
transcript:
Alex Reed: Thanks for making time. After the webinar you mentioned SDRs were drowning in research — can you walk me through the current workflow?
Jordan Blake: Sure. We are hiring into a mid-market warehouse motion and pipeline is the constraint. AEs can run late-stage deals; we are not generating enough qualified first meetings.
Sam Rivera: My team spends maybe two hours a day just finding emails and verifying titles. We bounce a lot. LinkedIn plus spreadsheets plus whatever is already in Salesforce — which is often stale.
Alex Reed: What does that look like for a typical account?
Sam Rivera: Say a regional 3PL. We need the VP Ops or Head of Warehouse Systems, plus whoever owns automation budget. Half the time the contact in Salesforce left six months ago.
Casey Nguyen: From Sales Ops side, enrichment is inconsistent. People overwrite fields, duplicates creep in, and we do not have a clean push back into Salesforce. I care about CRM hygiene as much as the prospecting UI.
Alex Reed: If this worked, what would change in the next quarter?
Jordan Blake: If SDRs spent less time researching and more time actually working sequences, we could lift meetings booked. I do not have a precise dollar model yet, but overtime on research and missed coverage on mid-market accounts is real. For a pilot I can fund from my sales budget; a broader rollout would need Finance and I have not looped them in.
Sam Rivera: I would use this every day if the data is decent and it does not create more Salesforce mess. Happy to be the day-to-day owner for an SDR pilot.
Alex Reed: Anyone else you are evaluating?
Jordan Blake: We tried a cheaper contact-only vendor last year and it did not stick. Nothing active right now besides improving our own lists.
Alex Reed: Next step — I can send a short workflow one-pager for SDR research plus Salesforce write-back, and we schedule a pilot scoping call?
Jordan Blake: Yes. Let's aim for later this month or early November. Sam and Casey should be there.
summary: October 14 discovery: Meridian Sales and SDR leadership described clear pain — manual prospect research, bounced/outdated contacts, and weak mid-market outbound coverage. Sales Ops needs clean Salesforce enrichment. Jordan can pilot from sales budget; Finance not engaged for broader purchase. Next step is a workflow one-pager and pilot scoping call (targeted late October / early November).
action_items: AE to send SDR workflow + Salesforce write-back one-pager.
Schedule pilot scoping call with Jordan, Sam, and Casey (late October / early November).
Capture draft pilot success ideas (research time saved, meetings booked) without fabricating ROI.
fixture_note: SYNTHETIC Granola-style fixture (not live Granola). Apollo ICP discovery for SCENARIO-01 CREATE. Dated Oct 2026 for a Nov 16, 2026 demo.

title: Discovery — Cascade Health Hospital Account Buying Groups
transcript:
Alex Reed: Thanks for the intro. What prompted looking at sales intelligence?
Avery Patel: Our AEs sell into hospital systems and larger clinic groups. Finding the right people is painful — operations, IT, and clinical stakeholders — and our CRM contacts are a mess.
Riley Chen: I am on the phones every day. I burn time guessing titles. Bounce rates are high. Sometimes I reach a manager who says the budget owner is someone else entirely.
Alex Reed: Have you measured the impact?
Riley Chen: Not formally. I just know I work fewer accounts thoroughly than I should. Avery hears it in pipeline reviews, but we do not have a clean baseline metric pack.
Alex Reed: Who would own a purchase if you moved forward?
Avery Patel: Unclear. Sales cares. RevOps would have to bless Salesforce changes — Quinn was not available today. Finance has not been involved. I am interested, but I am not opening a formal evaluation this week.
Alex Reed: Timeline?
Avery Patel: Maybe something exploratory later. Q4 is packed with year-end deals. Do not assume we have a deal process yet.
Riley Chen: I would love better contact data and a way to map buying groups on hospital accounts. I am not ready to champion an RFP.
Alex Reed: Any other vendors?
Avery Patel: We have not started a comparison. Separately someone mentioned enriching partner-referral leads, but that is a different thread — not what we are talking about today.
Alex Reed: I can send a short brief on contact enrichment and buying-group mapping for provider accounts. Would that help internal conversations?
Avery Patel: Yes. I will socialize it. Please do not treat this as a committed opportunity yet.
summary: October 21 early discovery: Cascade Sales and an SDR described legitimate pain finding hospital buying groups and keeping CRM contacts accurate. Metrics, Economic Buyer, decision process, and timeline remain undefined — Q4 bandwidth is limited. Avery will socialize a brief; no evaluation commitment. Distinct from the separate partner-lead enrichment thread tracked as OPP-002.
action_items: AE to send brief on contact enrichment and buying-group mapping for hospital/clinic accounts.
Avery to socialize internally and identify whether a budget owner exists.
Revisit after Cascade year-end capacity opens; no firm date committed.
fixture_note: SYNTHETIC Granola-style fixture (not live Granola). SCENARIO-02 CREATE WITH GAPS. Not a duplicate of OPP-002. Dated Oct 2026.

title: Follow-up — Meridian Robotics Apollo Sales Intelligence Platform
transcript:
Alex Reed: Picking up on the Apollo Sales Intelligence Platform proposal — where are we?
Jordan Blake: Still moving. This is the same platform evaluation we have been running for the AE team and Salesforce enrichment — not a new project. Separate from the SDR contact-data pilot we started talking about earlier this month.
Casey Nguyen: Security questionnaire is about 70% done. I need the Salesforce field-mapping diagram updated for the second sales region.
Sam Rivera: Acceptance criteria should still include bounce-rate improvement and usable mobile numbers for sequences. That has not changed.
Alex Reed: Should we open a separate opportunity for the second region?
Jordan Blake: Please do not. Keep it under the same Apollo Sales Intelligence Platform deal. Finance will get confused if there are two opportunities for one platform decision.
Alex Reed: Understood. I will revise pricing options for 25 vs 40 seats and the enrichment volume tiers.
Jordan Blake: Good. I will try to get Finance on a review after we see the update — ideally before year-end.
Casey Nguyen: Competitor-wise we are not in a bake-off; it is mostly Apollo versus improving our messy Salesforce data manually.
Alex Reed: Next step is the updated proposal and confirming the finance review.
Jordan Blake: Yes.
summary: October 28 follow-up on the existing Apollo Sales Intelligence Platform evaluation already in proposal stage (OPP-001). Stakeholders explicitly want one commercial platform initiative, not a second Opportunity, and distinguish it from the separate SDR contact-data pilot. Security questionnaire in progress; proposal revision and finance review are next.
action_items: AE to send updated Apollo platform proposal with seat and enrichment tiers.
Casey to continue security questionnaire with updated Salesforce field mapping.
Jordan to schedule Finance review after proposal revision (target before year-end).

title: Networking — Northwind Retail Group Intro Coffee

Alex Reed: Anything bubbling as a problem worth solving later?
Taylor Brooks: Nothing I would call a project. If something comes up it would be much later, and it would not be a discovery motion right now.
Morgan Ellis: (joining briefly) Hey — just saying hello. Hard stop on my side. Nice to meet you, Alex.
Alex Reed: Nice to meet you as well.
Morgan Ellis: Carry on — I am not here for a business discussion.
Taylor Brooks: Happy to stay connected. If you have a useful industry newsletter, send it. Otherwise coffee again when you are in Chicago.
Alex Reed: Sounds good. No product demo, no expansion proposal — just stay in touch?
Taylor Brooks: Exactly. Networking only.

title: Follow-up — Meridian Robotics SDR Pilot Scoping
transcript:

Jordan Blake: Yeah. Same SDR contact-data initiative we started then. Still interested. Still not the AE platform deal — that is the separate proposal track.
Sam Rivera: I can put four SDRs on a 60-day pilot if the data quality is decent. Day-to-day owner is still me. We have not started anything yet — no Salesforce Opportunity on our side that I know of for this pilot.
Casey Nguyen: I still need an explicit field-mapping diagram before any write-back. I can support a staged pilot; I do not own budget.
Alex Reed: Has anything changed on budget or timing since October?
Jordan Blake: Pilot funding from my sales budget is still fine. Finance is still not engaged for a broader rollout. Ideal start would be early January after the holiday push — not this month.
Sam Rivera: Success for me is less research time per account and fewer bounces into sequences. I still do not have a formal baseline export ready.
Alex Reed: Any new vendors in the mix?
Jordan Blake: No. Still Apollo versus status quo. Please do not merge this into the platform Opportunity — different buying motion.
Alex Reed: Next step — confirm pilot scope (four SDRs, Salesforce write-back staging) and whether you want me to open a Salesforce Opportunity for this SDR pilot now.
Jordan Blake: Yes on scope. On the Opportunity — if you have not created one yet, we should so my team can track it. Just keep it separate from the AE platform deal.

Finance still not engaged; metrics still informal. Explicitly distinct from the open AE-platform Opportunity. Jordan asks for a Salesforce Opportunity if one does not already exist — Skill should confirm initiative status before creating.
